title: Screening where the cone of vision captures an existing dwelling's opening
text: Notwithstanding C3.9.1, where the cone of vision captures a major opening or an active habitable space of an existing dwelling behind the greater of the street setback or street setback line on an adjoining property, the source of overlooking is designed to limit or interrupt the line of sight into the major opening or active habitable space of the adjoining property through one or more of the following: i. incorporate a permanent, fixed vertical or horizontal building element such as a planter box, fin or window hood (refer Figure 3.9c, Figure 3.9d); ii. have permanent, obscure glazing in any part of the window below 1.6m above floor level (refer Figure 3.9e); or iii. have permanent screening that is a minimum 75 per cent obscure to any part of the window or active habitable space below 1.6m above floor level (refer Figure 3.9f).

exceptions.label: cone falls forward of the adjoining property's street setback or street setback line, whichever is greater

replaces.note: trigger refined to 'behind the greater of the street setback or street setback line'

notes: from: ch3 C3.10.2 (renumbered C3.9.2). privacy.screened_or_offset covers limbs (i)-(iii) and the C3.9.3 offset. Not required where the cone falls forward of the greater of the adjoining street setback or street setback line. Applies to sources with a floor level more than 0.5 m above NGL; the cone radius includes the width of any adjoining ROW, communal street or battleaxe leg (p45 note). C3.9.4 applies C3.9.1-C3.9.3 between apartments on the same lot.
